newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa slides to new 9-mth low.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa slides to new 9-mth low.

text.p: London cocoa futures dropped to fresh nine-month lows on Friday as trade and origin sales weighed heavier in thin trading conditions during extended Christmas holidays.

The crucial 899 stg support was taken out with little hesitation, triggering light fund sales. The benchmark March contract then hit a low of 888 a tonne in the afternoon, clearing the ground for a further assault on 880.
"There are some shipping declarations. The industry are getting the cocoa and selling their futures," said one trader.
"A lot of industry buyers are away. In the meantime you're getting origin selling. We're finding better selling than buying," said another.
Sterling's strength against the French franc was said to have played a role in activating origins, mainly Ivory Coast.
A double-bottom formation at 899 was regarded as a strong technical base against further losses, but chart analysts are now looking at the 883-880 area for support.
"A close below 900 stg would likely see the lower target, 880 stg achieved with ease," said Elli Gifford, technical analyst at Investment Research of Cambridge.
The day's volume reached a relatively healthy 3,492 lots but traders said a large chunk was in crosses and AAs.
Many players have taken the day off to bridge Christmas holidays with a long weekend.
